seoTitle: 🫸 Rightwards Pushing Hand Emoji Meaning - What Does 🫸 Really Mean?
seoDescription: Learn what the rightwards pushing hand emoji 🫸 really means in texts and social media.

longForm.overview:
The 🫸 Rightwards Pushing Hand emoji was added in Unicode 14 (2021) and is drawn as a yellow hand with the palm facing forward in a stop gesture, fingers together, positioned as if pushing something away. The visual cue reads instantly as 'stop,' refusing, or the visible-'no thank you' tag. By 2026 🫸 has become the go-to emoji for the stop-and-refuse reaction, the visible-'I am pushing this away' tag, and the palm-coded-refusal default.

In modern chat 🫸 does very specific work. People send it as a literal pushing-away feeling, as the visible 'no thank you' tag, or as the palm-coded-refusal default. The palm-out-stop-gesture is the visual cue that the message is refusing. Writers should pick 🫸 when the read is stop or refuse, and avoid it when the read is different — 🙅 fits better for the universal no-coded default.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🫸 lands on a friend's 'no way' message, in a work channel where someone is refusing a request, and in a dating-app DM where the sender is pushing something away. The palm-out-stop-gesture anchors the read.

In close-friends chats 🫸 reads as the universal 'I am pushing this away' tag and the palm-coded-refusal default. On X the emoji punctuates refusing-coded tweets. The emoji pairs with 🙅 for the layered refuse-and-no-pair stack and with 🙅‍♂️ for the layered palm-and-no-person stack.
longForm.whenNotToUse: Skip 🫸 in any context where the read is purely no-coded universal — 🙅 fits better. Avoid 🫸 in ironic contexts where the refusing is faked — 🙄 fits better there.
longForm.howToReply:
If a friend sends 🫸 on a refuse message, mirror with a sentence that respects the refuse. The pushing-hand chain needs an acknowledgment.

If 🫸 lands as the 'no thanks' default, reply with a sentence that respects the boundary. And if you want to send 🫸 yourself, pair it with the moment so the refusing read is clear.

faqs.question: What does 🫸 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 🫸 means 'stop,' refusing, or 'I am pushing this away.' The palm-out-stop-gesture is the visual cue that the message is refusing.

faqs.question: What does 🫸 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: From a guy or anyone, 🫸 carries the same refuse read. There is no gendered meaning; the emoji works the same regardless.

faqs.question: Is 🫸 passive aggressive?
faqs.answer: Sometimes. 🫸 can read as visibly-pushing-something-away in a passive context. Watch the surrounding context for the read.

faqs.question: What does 🫸 mean at work?
faqs.answer: In Slack, 🫸 reads as the 'I am pushing this back' tag for a problematic request. Pair with a clarifying sentence about why so the channel stays useful.
